channel.title: The Berkshire Edge - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Berkshire Edge (theberkshireedge.com)

item.title: Great Barrington Selectboard and Finance Committee review capital requests at budget meeting
item.description: With Town Manager Liz Hartsgrove proposing a $17.3 million budget and a Proposition 2½ override, a Finance Committee member says residents are telling her they can no longer afford their taxes.

item.title: Great Barrington Public Theater announces its 2026 summer season
item.description: “We’ll present a season of world-premiere plays at a newly configured, intimate black box theater in the Great Hall at Saint James Place, with upgraded lighting and seating elements to create a unique space to embrace these provocative new plays,” says co-Artistic Director Jim Frangione.

item.title: An empty chair by Section 9 at Tanglewood
item.description: Although Lou’s Section 9 chair will be occupied by others in coming seasons, for us who loved him, we will always remember it as the seat of the “Mayor of Tanglewood.”

item.title: Borscht for Ukraine fundraiser at Dewey Hall brings community together, raises more than $25,000 for relief efforts in Ukraine
item.description: Razom, which means “together” in Ukrainian, seemed to be a theme of the afternoon as attendees shared their hopes and prayers for the Ukrainian people, made all the more resonant by the bombing of Iran that morning.

item.title: Rollout of smart meters in Berkshires prompts discussions from local governing boards, community members
item.description: Experts and town officials tout radiofrequency education as the first step in understanding the issue.

item.title: Berkshire Lyric presents ‘Celebrating America’s Musical Roots at 250’
item.description: Jack Brown leads The Berkshire Lyric Chorus, the Lyric Children’s Chorus, and Melodious Accord, with accompaniment from Joe Rose.

item.title: PETER MOST: The new Community Preservation Act
item.description: A new state designation under the Affordable Homes Act could give Great Barrington voluntary tools to preserve year-round housing for essential workers—but only if voters say yes at Annual Town Meeting.

item.title: BITS & BYTES: Amber Chand at Spencertown Academy; Crescendo at Saint James Place; ‘Women in Art’ at the Licht; WordXWord’s Poets Creating Conversation; Zonta Club scholarship; Stockbridge Grange community dinner
item.description: “Amber is a spellbinding storyteller. Exploring themes of wisdom, beauty, and humanity, she transports us to distant lands through her tales,” says Academy Administrator Eve Zatt.

item.title: THE LAZY BERKSHIRE GARDENER: Week of March 5, 2026
item.description: I suppose that most of us will still have a foot or more of snow on the ground this weekend. Are you eager to sow some seeds?

item.title: THE SELF-TAUGHT GARDENER: What lies beneath
item.description: On a trip to the Galanthus Gala in Pennsylvania, more snow and the hope of spring cause this gardener to wonder what comes next.
